order: get to a safe place first
listen to warnings from the emergency services
safety: after an earthquake, call only if someone needs help: keep the lines free

little.twist: The shaking starts by the window, and nothing glows.
little.can_now: drop, cover and hold on in an earthquake, go indoors in thunder, and stay put if they get lost

steps.say: The practice room. Sometimes the ground shakes: that's an earthquake. {quake_where} The rule: never run outside while it shakes. Drop, cover, hold on.

steps.late: Drop down now: onto your hands and knees.
steps.say: It's shaking! Drop down onto your hands and knees.

steps.late: Drop down now: onto your hands and knees.
steps.say: You're by the window and it starts to shake! Drop!
Cover: crawl under the strong table.
steps.done: Under the table: it protects you.

steps.say: Away from the window: where is safe?
steps.done: Under the strong table, away from the glass.

steps.say: Hold on to the table leg until the shaking stops.
The shaking stopped. What now?

choices.text: Wait for my grown-up, then go out together

choices.why: Stay calm and wait for your grown-up: they take you out.

steps.done: Gus comes to take you out to open ground.

steps.say: You can stand up now. Walk out with Gus to the open grass, away from buildings and trees.
Later, in the park, a storm comes: dark clouds and thunder.
Thunder! Where do you go?

choices.why: Lightning can strike a tall tree. Go inside.

steps.say: Practice: you're on a walk in the woods and you can't see your grown-up.
Stay where you are: hug a tree.
steps.done: Hugging a tree: staying put helps them find you.

steps.say: You hear your name! What do you do?

choices.why: Answer! The people calling are helpers looking for you.

steps.say: Shaking: drop, cover, hold on. Thunder: go indoors. Lost: stay put, hug a tree, and answer when they call.

choices.text: Stay put and hug a tree

name_it.title: Shake, storm, lost
lines: Ground shaking: drop, cover, hold on.
Never run outside while it shakes.
Lost? Stay put, hug a tree, and answer when they call.
name_it.source: The ShakeOut earthquake drill, the US National Weather Service and Hug-a-Tree and Survive

little.try_real: With a grown-up: find the strongest table at home to shelter under, and practise drop, cover, hold on together.

sources.fact: In an earthquake: Drop onto your hands and knees, Cover your head and neck (under a sturdy table if one is near), Hold On until the shaking stops; don't run outside.
sources.source: Earthquake Country Alliance, ShakeOut: Drop, Cover, Hold On

sources.fact: Georgia's own guidance for an earthquake and other emergencies, and its 112.
When thunder roars, go indoors; never shelter under a tree.
sources.source: US National Weather Service, lightning safety

sources.fact: A child lost outdoors should stay in one place, hug a tree, and answer when people call.
sources.source: Hug-a-Tree and Survive (a US children's programme, 1981)

middle.twist: No table this time: find the safest place by yourself.
middle.can_now: drop, cover and hold on, keep out of flood water, and stay safe in thunder and heat

steps.say: The practice room. Today: an earthquake, a flood, lightning and a hot day. {quake_where}

steps.late: Drop straight away: onto your hands and knees.
steps.say: It's shaking! Drop!

safe_mistake.why: While it shakes, the floor moves under your feet, and tiles and glass can fall by doors and windows. Down low, under something strong, is safest.
safe_mistake.right: Drop, cover under the table, and hold on until it stops.

steps.say: Cover: get under something strong.
Hold on until the shaking stops.

steps.late: Cover quickly, by a wall away from the window.

safe_mistake.why: While it shakes, the floor moves under your feet, and tiles and glass can fall by doors and windows. Down low, inside, is safest.
safe_mistake.right: No table? Get down by an inside wall, away from the window, and cover your head and neck.

steps.say: No table here today. Where is safest?
steps.done: By the inside wall, away from the glass.

steps.say: Cover your head and neck with your arms, and hold on until it stops.
You can stand up. Walk out with your grown-up, don't run.
To open ground, away from buildings, trees and power lines.
steps.done: Safe in the open. If anyone is hurt, a grown-up calls {number}.

steps.say: A smaller shake: an aftershock. Out here, get down and cover your head and neck with your arms.
After heavy rain, fast water flows across the path. What do you do?

choices.why: Just 15 cm of fast water can knock you over. Never walk, play or cycle in flood water.
Fast water can sweep a bike away. Turn around.

steps.done: Turn around: never into flood water.

steps.say: Thunder on the football field! Where do you go?

choices.text: Inside a building or a car

choices.why: Lightning often strikes tall things like a lone tree.
Lying down doesn't keep you safe. Get inside.

steps.say: A very hot day. What keeps you well?

choices.why: Play in the shade, drink water, and rest in the hottest part of the day.

steps.say: Shaking: drop, cover, hold on, then open ground. Flood water: turn around. Thunder: get inside. Heat: shade, water and rest.

choices.text: Stay inside: drop, cover, hold on
Get down by an inside wall, cover your head

name_it.title: Earth and weather
lines: Shaking: drop, cover, hold on. Never run out while it shakes.
Afterwards: walk out to open ground, away from buildings, trees and power lines.
Flood water: turn around, never walk or ride through it.
Thunder: get inside a building or a car, never under a lone tree.
name_it.source: ShakeOut, FEMA's Ready.gov, the US National Weather Service, the UK Environment Agency and the WHO (heat and health)

middle.try_real: With a grown-up: find the safe spots at home (under a strong table, by an inside wall) and the open place outside where your family would meet.

sources.fact: Drop, Cover, Hold On; if there is no table, get down by an interior wall and cover your head and neck; stay away from windows; don't run outside during shaking.
Georgia's earthquake and emergency guidance, and the 112 service.
sources.source: Emergency Management Service of Georgia; 112 Georgia

sources.fact: After the shaking: expect aftershocks (drop, cover, hold on again); go to open space away from buildings, trees and power lines.
Turn Around, Don't Drown: never walk, swim or drive through flood water; 15 cm of moving water can knock you down.
sources.source: US National Weather Service, flood safety

sources.fact: Just 30 cm of flowing water can float a car, and 15 cm of fast water can knock you off your feet.
sources.source: UK Environment Agency, what to do in a flood

sources.fact: When thunder roars, go indoors: a building or a hard-topped car; never under a lone tree.
sources.source: US National Weather Service, lightning safety

sources.fact: In heat: keep out of the sun in the hottest hours, drink water, rest in the shade.

big.twist: The shaking starts outside: find the clear space by yourself.
big.can_now: pack an emergency bag, shelter safely in an earthquake, and stay safe and easy to find in storms and the hills

steps.say: The practice house. Being ready comes first. {quake_where}

steps.label: In the bag
steps.say: Pack your family's emergency bag: water, a torch, a whistle, first aid, warm layers and food that keeps. It holds 10 spaces.
steps.done: Packed and ready by the door.

steps.say: Days later, it starts shaking while you're by the window. Drop!

steps.late: Cover quickly, away from the window.

safe_mistake.why: While it shakes, the floor moves under your feet, and tiles and glass can fall by doors and windows. Down low, under something strong, is safest.
safe_mistake.right: Away from the window: drop, cover under the table, and hold on.

steps.say: Away from the glass: cover.
steps.done: Under the table, away from the window.

steps.say: Hold on until the shaking stops.
You can stand up. Put on your shoes before you walk: there may be broken glass.
Walk out with your family, and take the emergency bag.
To open ground: away from buildings, trees and power lines.
steps.done: Safe in the open. If someone is hurt, call {number}; otherwise keep the phone lines free.

steps.say: Days later, you're outside by the school when it starts shaking.

steps.late: Quickly: to the clear space if you safely can.

safe_mistake.wrong: running into a building during the shaking
safe_mistake.why: Tiles and glass can fall by doorways and walls while it shakes. Outside, a clear space away from buildings is safest.
safe_mistake.right: Move to a clear space if you safely can, away from buildings, trees and wires, then drop and cover.

steps.say: Where is safest out here?
steps.done: In the clear space, away from walls, trees and wires.

steps.say: Drop, and cover your head and neck with your arms until it stops.
Later, on a walk in the hills, a thunderstorm comes.
Thunder in the hills. What do you do?

choices.text: Go down, away from peaks, lone trees and water, and get inside
Shelter under the lone tree on top
choices.why: Lightning strikes high, tall things. Go down and get inside a building or a car.

choices.text: Stand on the hilltop to watch
choices.why: High, open places are where lightning strikes. Go down and get inside.

steps.done: Down and inside: a building or a car.

steps.say: Practice: you've lost the path and your family in the woods.
What do you do first?

choices.text: Keep walking to find the way
choices.why: Moving makes you harder to find. Stay put: searchers look where you were.

steps.done: Stay put: it's easier for them to find you.

steps.say: Stay by a big tree.
Make yourself easy to see: put on your bright jacket.
Make yourself easy to hear: blow your whistle, again and again. It carries further than a voice.
It's getting cold and wet. What helps?

choices.text: Layers, a hat, and keep dry

choices.why: Sit on your bag or a log, keep dry, put your layers and hat on.

steps.done: Warm layers, a hat, dry: and they find you.

steps.say: A heatwave in summer. What keeps everyone well?

choices.text: Shade, water, rest, and never leave anyone in a parked car

choices.why: Rest in the hottest hours, drink water, and check on babies and older neighbours.

steps.say: Ready first: an emergency bag and a plan. Shaking: drop, cover, hold on. Thunder: down and inside. Lost: stay put, be seen and heard. Cold: layers. Heat: shade and water.

choices.text: Water, a torch, a whistle, first aid, warm layers

check.say: It shakes while you're by a window...

choices.text: Away from it, under a table, hold on

check.say: After the shaking, before you walk...

choices.text: Shoes on: there may be broken glass
Stay put, be seen and heard

name_it.title: Ready for anything
lines: Be ready: an emergency bag and a family plan.
Drop, cover, hold on; shoes on before you walk; then out to open ground.
Thunder: go down, away from peaks, lone trees and water, and get inside.
Lost: stay put, be seen (bright colours) and heard (a whistle).
Cold: layers, a hat, keep dry. Heat: shade, water, rest.
name_it.source: ShakeOut, FEMA's Ready.gov, the US National Weather Service, mountain rescue advice and Hug-a-Tree and Survive

big.try_real: With a grown-up: pack (or check) your family's emergency bag together, and agree where you would all meet.

sources.fact: A basic emergency kit: water, food that keeps, a torch, a whistle to signal for help, a first aid kit, warm clothes, and a family plan.
After an earthquake, wear sturdy shoes: there may be broken glass and debris.
Outdoors in an earthquake: move to a clear area if you safely can, away from buildings, trees and power lines; drop, cover, hold on.
Georgia's own earthquake and emergency guidance, and its 112 service.
Lightning: no place outside is safe; get off peaks and away from lone trees and water, and into a building or a hard-topped car.
sources.source: US National Weather Service, lightning safety

sources.fact: Lost: stay where you are, keep warm and dry, make yourself seen (bright colours) and heard (a whistle).
sources.source: Mountain Rescue England and Wales, advice; Hug-a-Tree and Survive

sources.fact: Heat: stay out of the hottest sun, drink water, and never leave anyone in a parked car.
